# Daily Stripe reconciliation

> Every night at 02:30 UTC, this job streams Stripe charges from that day, compares them with our payment records by idempotency key, and records any mismatches for investigation.

_Part of [domain/payments](../../units/domain/payments.md)_

Every morning Stripe and our system should agree on what was charged. The `payments.reconcile-daily` job runs at 02:30 UTC to check this. It streams Stripe's payment intents for the previous day, loads our `COMPLETED` payments for that day, and matches them by idempotency key—the unique request ID we send to Stripe with each charge. When they disagree—a charge with no matching payment record, a payment we recorded but Stripe never confirmed, or different amounts—the job records the mismatch as a `ReconciliationIssue` for the finance team to investigate. The job is idempotent: once a day's reconciliation finishes, re-running it does nothing; if it crashes mid-way, starting it over clears the incomplete issues and tries again. Each run is tracked in `ReconciliationRun`, keyed by (provider='stripe', day). The job streams Stripe results to keep memory flat regardless of volume, but loads all our `COMPLETED` payments for the day into a map for quick lookup by idempotency key.

**Look at:** [`ReconciliationJobs` in reconciliation.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/reconciliation.jobs.ts#L24)

## Pieces

- Reconciliation run tracking and issue records: `ReconciliationRun` tracks one reconciliation attempt per (provider, day); `ReconciliationIssue` records each mismatch with kind, payment reference, and details.
- Three types of reconciliation mismatches: `MISSING_IN_LEDGER` means Stripe charged but we have no payment record; `MISSING_AT_PROVIDER` means we recorded a payment but Stripe never confirmed it; `AMOUNT_MISMATCH` means both exist but amounts differ.
- [Matching payments by idempotency key](idempotency-key-matching.md): Payments are matched across Stripe and our records using the idempotency key—the request ID we send to Stripe with the charge. Stripe stores it in `payment_intent.metadata.idempotencyKey`; we store it in the `Payment` record. Charges without an idempotency ke…
- Streaming Stripe charges to avoid memory overflow: The job calls `StripeService.paymentIntentsCreatedBetween()` to iterate over charges one by one instead of fetching all at once, keeping memory flat. Periodically it calls `ctx.heartbeat()` to refresh the job lease.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | ```ReconciliationRun`` table` | Upserted once per (provider, day); tracks each reconciliation attempt with id, provider, day, `finishedAt`, matched count, and issue count. Used to detect if reconciliation already finished (for idempotency) and to delete stale issues on retry. |
| database | ```ReconciliationIssue`` table` | Inserted once per mismatch; stores `runId`, kind (`MISSING_IN_LEDGER`, `MISSING_AT_PROVIDER`, or `AMOUNT_MISMATCH`), payment reference, and details JSON. Cleared fresh each run. |
| database | ``Payment` table` | Queried to load all COMPLETED payments for the target day, indexed by idempotency key. Compared against Stripe charges. |
| external | `Stripe API` | Streamed via `StripeService.paymentIntentsCreatedBetween()` to get all payment intents created on the target day. Only succeeded intents are considered; their amount and `metadata.idempotencyKey` are extracted. |
| job | ```payments.reconcile-daily``` | Scheduled cron job: `30 2 * * *` (02:30 UTC every day). Concurrency: 1 (only one runs at a time). Lease timeout: 600 seconds with heartbeat. |

## Watch out

- Idempotency key must be set in Stripe's `payment_intent.metadata.idempotencyKey` or the charge will be skipped entirely; unmatched charges never appear in our records.
- If reconciliation crashes mid-way, re-running it clears all old issues for that day and starts fresh—there is no checkpoint or partial progress.
- Issues are recorded but never auto-fixed; the finance team must investigate and correct discrepancies manually (e.g., by adjusting ledger entries).
- The job loads all our `COMPLETED` payments for the entire day into a map, so very high-volume days could spike memory usage on the application side (though Stripe streaming keeps its side constant).
